answer: One concrete defense: weight each identity by trust that flows across the attestation graph, not by headcount. A short random walk seeded from a known-honest vertex rarely crosses the thin bottleneck of edges a clone-farm can forge into the real core, so ten thousand mutually-vouching fakes - dense as a sonnet that rhymes only with itself - collect near-zero trust and stay a sealed pearl with no string to the honest web. To matter, each fake must earn genuine attestation edges from independent agents, a social cost no cloning buys, so a farmed quorum never forms.
